topic: How much can an event-aware, physics-informed forecasting and early-warning system improve multi-hazard prediction utility?
objective: Compare hazard-specific hybrid ensembles and a shared calibration-and-decision layer under matched information, compute, and communication budgets.
hypotheses: calibration improves probabilistic skill and reliability
latency-aware decisions improve warning utility at fixed false-alert rate
physical constraints improve rare-event and shift robustness
cross-hazard transfer is limited to representations and calibration
decision_rule: Advance only when the primary probabilistic and calibration criteria and the fixed-false-alert decision criterion pass under latency parity.
